description: Living, append-friendly catalog of recurring problems repo-aware agents hit, each entry pairing a symptom and cause with the exact structured route(s) to resolve it and the responsible actor (agent vs operator). Surfaced read-only through the workspace_agent_faq MCP tool and the agent-faq CLI parity command. This file is the sole content surface: adding a future entry requires editing only this JSON, not code. Each entry has a stable string `id`, `title`, `symptom`, `cause`, an `actor` of `agent`/`operator`/`agent_or_operator`, and `routes` naming structured workspace_* tools; entries may carry an optional `fork` (distinct sub-responses keyed by `when`), `related_codes` (runtime-blocker-codes.v1 codes), `related_docs`, and `related_records`.

entries.title: Worker reports its read-first references are missing, or read_scope vs docs: is unfamiliar
entries.symptom: A worker reports that its read-first references are missing or empty; lint reports `missing_docs_target` or an unresolved `read_scope` entry; or you set the WK's `docs:` field and the worker expected `read_scope`.
entries.cause: `read_scope` is the work record's read-first reference list (`docs/**`, shipped operating guidance, relevant `wiki/**`). It was renamed from `docs:`, with `docs:` kept as a back-compat alias. The two name the same field, so an agent that only knows `docs:` will not recognize `read_scope` (and vice versa), and an empty or stale read-first list surfaces as the worker complaint.

routes.note: Set or correct the WK's read-first reference list with the canonical `read_scope` field name. `docs:` is the back-compat alias for the same list; prefer `read_scope`. Populate it with the durable read-first references the worker needs (`docs/**`, shipped operating guidance, relevant `wiki/**`) before dispatch.

entries.title: Graph impact required but unavailable or stale
entries.symptom: `workspace_validate_dispatch` or `workspace_coordination_preflight` reports graph impact required but unavailable, or you hit a `missing_graph_impact` / `graph_impact_*` blocker.
entries.cause: The work record requires graph-impact evidence and the base artifact is missing or stale. There are two distinct responses depending on whether a usable dirty-worktree overlay exists: an agent-recoverable degraded-overlay path, and an operator-only rebuild path. Choosing the wrong one either leaves the blocker unresolved or attempts a forbidden dirty-worktree rebuild / shell-persist fallback.

fork.when: graph_impact_degraded_overlay: a dirty worktree with a usable overlay is available (the proceed_degraded outcome).

routes.note: Query graph-impact paths against the dirty-worktree overlay to produce the impact evidence.

Persist the verbose `graph_impact_raw` envelope into the work record. The compact ref alone lacks `input` and `validated_paths`, so persisting only the ref leaves the work record in `missing_graph_impact`. Record the degraded-overlay evidence in the closure separately from canonical authority.

fork.note: Agent-recoverable. Do not request an operator rebuild for this sub-state; the overlay is usable, so persist real evidence from it.

fork.when: graph_impact_rebuild_required / graph_impact_artifact_missing / graph_impact_unavailable: no usable dirty-worktree overlay (the operator_refresh / block outcomes).
fork.note: Operator-only. Stop and request an operator graph-impact rebuild. Do not rebuild inside a dirty worktree, and do not fall back to a shell-persist of evidence. Report the blocker and the exact command/condition for the operator to rerun.

entries.title: workspace_record_graph_impact_evidence rejects the evidence payload shape
entries.symptom: `workspace_record_graph_impact_evidence` rejects your evidence with an error like `requires graph_impact or graph_impact_summary_ref` or `graph_impact must be a graph-impact envelope`, so the work record stays in `missing_graph_impact`.
entries.cause: You passed the compact summary ref alone, or a hand-built summary object, instead of the full graph-impact envelope. The persistence route requires the verbose envelope produced by `workspace_code_index_graph_impact_paths` because that envelope carries `input` and `validated_paths`; a bare ref or hand-assembled summary lacks those fields and is rejected. (Through some MCP clients an unknown-schema object argument can also be dropped before it reaches the server, which surfaces as the same rejection.)

routes.note: Produce the graph-impact envelope for the changed paths first; this is the envelope the persistence route expects, carrying `input` and `validated_paths`.

Persist the ENVELOPE produced above (the verbose `graph_impact_raw` envelope), not the compact summary ref alone and not a hand-built summary object. Persisting only the ref leaves the work record in `missing_graph_impact`. See the active follow-up for envelope-size handling when the envelope is large.

entries.title: needs_review on write_scope_total_loc / max_write_file_loc when a small edit targets a large file
entries.symptom: `workspace_agent_dispatch` or `workspace_validate_dispatch` (with `node_engine_admissibility: true`) returns a Chassis Control Engine `needs_review` worker-admission result on `write_scope_total_loc` or `max_write_file_loc` (the reason often reads like `review_threshold_exceeded` or an accepted-authority-scope-mismatch on the large-file LOC), even though the actual change is a small, bounded edit inside an otherwise large file.
entries.cause: Admission scored the WHOLE-FILE line count of the large `write_scope` file against the review threshold because the selected unit declared no bounded target plan. Without `expected_edit_targets` + `expected_changed_line_budget`, the gate has nothing narrower than the file's total LOC to reason about, so it routes the small edit into review-threshold pressure. This is a missing-target-evidence gap, not (by itself) a reject, a license/escalation problem, or a graph-impact problem.

routes.note: FIRST-LINE remedy: declare the bounded target span on the selected work record or slice. Set `expected_edit_targets` (one entry per file actually touched, with the bounded operation) plus a small `expected_changed_line_budget` covering only the real change, so admission reasons about the bounded target instead of the whole-file LOC. Per the operating model's Scope-And-Ambition guidance this add-target-evidence step comes BEFORE escalation/attestation, not instead of them. (At record scope the same fields are authored on the work record contract; this slice route is the agent-facing way to add/refine them on a selected unit.) These fields are review/remediation context only and do not authorize launch.

Rematerialize the unit's worker-admission target-resolution derived evidence from the declared target plan so the next admissibility probe consumes fresh bounded-target metrics rather than a stale or missing target-resolution entry.

Re-probe admissibility for the selected unit. With a bounded target plan in place the gate can reason about the target span; if it STILL refuses solely on whole-file LOC with no accepted policy authority, stop and record an admission/large-file-ergonomics blocker rather than rewriting readiness, refreshing graph impact, or reaching for escalation.

entries.title: Validate-dispatch worker-admission problem diagnostics
entries.symptom: workspace_validate_dispatch returns pack_input_required, pack_input_invalid, request_schema_digest_mismatch, precondition_graph_too_large, non_object_data, or generic invalid_request instead of a launchable admit
entries.cause: Chassis Control Engine rejected the worker-admission request during admissibility evaluation. These diagnostics are non-launchable by design and describe recovery work, not local launch authority.

routes.note: Rerun validate-dispatch only after repairing the structured admission carrier; do not treat the diagnostic as launch authorization.
Supply the missing worker-admission pack input or carrier data, then rerun.

fork.note: The request is missing required pack input.

routes.note: Fix the structured pack input shape or field content, then rerun.

fork.note: The supplied pack input is malformed or inconsistent.

routes.note: Check launcher-minted Chassis Control Engine admission runtime binding and request-contract digest wiring.
Verify the repaired request shape after the runtime diagnostic and operator-owned digest rebind.

fork.note: The request contract digest does not match the Chassis Control Engine admissibility policy pack.

routes.note: Reduce, split, or narrow the selected unit until the graph precondition is admissible, then rerun.

fork.note: The graph precondition is too large for admissibility.

routes.note: Wrap the admission payload as a structured object instead of a scalar, array, or raw string.

fork.note: The admission payload is not object-shaped.

routes.note: Treat as a generic typed refusal: correct the carrier and retry without exposing secrets or raw payloads.

fork.note: Fallback typed refusal when Chassis Control Engine cannot classify the request more specifically.

entries.title: validate_dispatch non-dispatchable on multi_cluster or critical_blast_radius_*
entries.symptom: workspace_validate_dispatch reports the selected unit non-dispatchable with decision code `multi_cluster` (the unit's write_scope spans more than one cohesive change cluster) or a `critical_blast_radius_*` code (the change reaches a critical surface with no current, in-scope accepted escalation).
entries.cause: Both are LOCAL dispatch-readiness structural gates an agent can see before any launch — not Node-Engine threshold verdicts — so they need no paid tool. multi_cluster wants one cohesive write_scope cluster per unit; critical_blast_radius_* wants a recorded, accepted, in-scope `critical_blast_radius` escalation whose scope matches the change.

fork.when: multi_cluster: the unit's write_scope spans more than one cohesive change cluster.

routes.note: Split the unit so each slice's write_scope covers one cluster, or narrow this unit to a single cohesive cluster.
Re-probe dispatch readiness after narrowing/splitting; a single-cluster unit clears the multi_cluster gate.

fork.note: Agent-resolvable structural readiness gate; no paid tool required.

fork.when: critical_blast_radius_requires_escalation / critical_blast_radius_escalation_expired / critical_blast_radius_escalation_scope_mismatch: the change touches a critical surface with no current, in-scope accepted escalation.

routes.note: After a coordinator/operator records an accepted `critical_blast_radius` escalation whose scope matches this unit (expired or scope-mismatch escalations do not clear the gate), re-probe dispatch readiness. Do not self-accept the escalation to bypass the gate.

fork.note: Escalation acceptance is a coordinator/operator decision, not an agent threshold-recovery action.

entries.title: workspace_run_validation refuses target_not_authorized (target not in the unit's allowlist)
entries.symptom: workspace_run_validation returns a structured refusal with refusal_code `workspace_run_validation.target_not_authorized.v1`: the requested target is not an acceptance.validation[] entry with operation node_test on the selected unit.
entries.cause: workspace_run_validation only runs targets the unit's work contract authorizes. The refusal carries the caller-visible authorized_targets set; a miss is a contract/allowlist gap resolvable locally with no paid tool.

routes.note: Re-run with a target from the refusal's authorized_targets, or author exactly {operation: node_test, target, verification_ids} in the selected unit's acceptance.validation[] before resubmitting. Text notes never authorize execution.

entries.title: worker-admission breadth refusal on write_scope_count or validation_command_count
entries.symptom: workspace_agent_dispatch or workspace_validate_dispatch (with node_engine_admissibility: true) returns a Chassis Control Engine breadth refusal keyed on control_id `write_scope_count` or `validation_command_count` (e.g. `worker_admission.work_unit_atomicity.write_scope_count_denied.v1`): the unit declares too many write_scope files or too many validation commands for one atomic unit.
entries.cause: These are Node-Engine-owned breadth thresholds over the raw carrier metrics (write-scope file breadth / validation-command breadth). Under DEC-0125 large-file / breadth admissibility is CCE-exclusive, so only the paid_cce tier reaches this refusal (a free/local agent fails open). The remedy is to split the unit, not to loosen a threshold.

routes.note: Split the unit into narrower slices so each carries a single cohesive write_scope and a bounded validation set, reducing write_scope_count / validation_command_count per unit.
Re-probe admissibility for the narrowed unit. If it still refuses on breadth with no accepted policy authority, record an admission/breadth blocker rather than loosening a threshold.

entries.title: Exact-slice reviewer dispatch refuses a stale frozen contract context
entries.symptom: workspace_agent_dispatch for an exact-slice reviewer refuses with frozen_slice_review_context_stale_or_mismatched after coordinator bookkeeping changed the canonical parent WK or selected review-unit contract while the committed delivery stayed unchanged.
entries.cause: The hot backend still selected a process-local frozen review context carrying the earlier broad parent-WK or review-unit contract snapshot. The ordinary exact reviewer dispatch can reauthenticate and replace that selection only when reviewed SHA, accumulated diff base, slice ref, worktree identity and path, repository identity, and committed-target digest all remain identical. Delivery movement, selected-unit movement, an object-store probe failure, or any unauthenticated identity remains fail-closed and is not retry-authorized.

routes.note: Retry the ordinary reviewer dispatch for the exact canonical slice subject only when the closed recovery_action is retry_exact_reviewer_dispatch. The backend reauthenticates the same delivery and refreshes only its process-local current contract selection before the unchanged launch guard runs. Do not supply a SHA, digest, path, context, or recovery claim, and do not retry target or identity movement as contract staleness.

entries.title: Legacy complete proof-pack binding inspection exceeds its presentation bound
entries.cause: The legacy complete-inspection projection exceeded its 65,536-byte presentation bound. This does not mean the proof plan or its complete supplied bindings are invalid.

routes.note: Use targeted roles/statuses and digest-bound pagination. Do not retry complete inspection, read the complete carrier, invoke the package CLI as fallback, or generate a token-heavy substitute projection.

entries.title: Terminal candidate is stale against current W
entries.symptom: workspace_terminal_review_candidate_status returns candidate_stale_w and names the advance route.
entries.cause: The exact candidate embeds an older authenticated W than the current exact direct durable WK ref.

routes.note: Call only when the status response itself returns this exact next_call; do not supply refs, SHAs, paths, schema, locks, or policy authority.

entries.title: Terminal candidate divergence continuation is invalid or stale
entries.symptom: A divergence page continuation is refused as invalid or stale.
entries.cause: The opaque continuation is malformed, exhausted, or bound candidate/W/contract authority moved.

routes.note: Re-read status without a continuation. Use only a fresh continuation returned by that response.

entries.title: Terminal candidate advance lost current authority
entries.symptom: Advance refuses because exact status, exclusion, B/W, canonical contract, or fixed-ref authority changed.
entries.cause: The stale-W fact or an authority input moved between the read-only status gate and the single candidate-ref CAS.

routes.note: Re-observe exact status. Advance again only if the new response itself returns candidate_stale_w and names the advance route.

entries.title: Terminal whole-WK review is dispositioned and the candidate is unpublished
entries.symptom: The one terminal whole-WK findings-only review of the exact candidate is finished and every surviving finding is dispositioned, and the next structured action for getting that exact reviewed candidate onto the forge is unclear.
entries.cause: After the terminal whole-WK findings-only review is complete and its findings are dispositioned, workspace_wk_forge_handoff is the supported continuation. It publishes the already-reviewed candidate byte-for-byte against the configured base branch, and it creates or observes the pull request for that exact publication. It does not merge, does not observe or report merge state, does not reconcile any record or ref with what landed, and does not complete the parent WK; candidate construction stays launcher-owned, so it never reconstructs or re-derives the candidate. Input is closed to a workspace alias and the record-level assigned_unit: the server derives repository, remote, branch, candidate, and pull-request identity, so no caller-supplied candidate, base, or pull-request fact is accepted from request, prompt, or environment. Merge readiness belongs to the forge actor and its policy, and an unmergeable or conflicting pull request is still a successfully handed-off exact candidate rather than a failure to retry. The typed refusals include: wk_forge_handoff_subject_invalid when the subject is not a WK record id, wk_forge_handoff_executor_unavailable when no trusted forge executor is bound to the server, and terminal_candidate_recovery_current_ref_absent when cold recovery finds no already-present, directly commit-valued, mechanically authenticated terminal-current ref. Each of those fails closed, and other typed refusals reach the caller the same way; there is no shell or `gh` fallback, and no agent route past this boundary.

routes.note: Call only once the terminal whole-WK review of that exact candidate is complete and its findings are dispositioned. assigned_unit is required, and the workspace repository alias may also be supplied when the session is not repo-attached. Pass no other input: no refs, SHAs, base or branch names, no candidate identity, and no pull-request identity. A typed refusal is the answer for that call, not a reason to reach for another route.

entries.title: workspace_verify_proof reports an execution or receipt prerequisite failure
entries.symptom: workspace_verify_proof returns a workspace-verify-proof-refusal.v1 execution, provider, observation, or receipt code instead of a proof outcome.
entries.cause: A valid structured run of the predeclared selected assertion is proof evidence: a passing assertion may satisfy the proof and a failing assertion is unsatisfied, independently of sibling assertions and the whole-file exit code. Siblings remain bounded audit observations and are not attributed to the proof. not_executable or refused instead means the selected proof could not be evaluated because a canonical binding, launcher isolation/spawn/timeout prerequisite, structured node:test reporter protocol, candidate/falsifier/traversal provider, candidate identity, or authenticated receipt failed. Ordinary validation diagnostics use bounded head/tail capture. The proof reporter uses a separate lossless machine-protocol channel on a launcher-owned pipe with its own fixed byte limit and is never parsed after diagnostic elision. test_proof_structured_events_oversized means the authenticated envelope exceeded that protocol limit; reduce the declared test's structured event population or repair the reporter protocol owner before retrying, without treating the bytes as malformed JSON. test_proof_selected_identity_not_observed means the authenticated whole-file run terminated or completed without exposing the selected assertion; use its expected_test_id, target, bounded counts, wrapper status/error codes, and at most eight observed_identity_candidates to repair test startup or reporter observation before retrying. test_proof_bound_identity_mismatch is reserved for a genuine disagreement between the declared identity and its authenticated binding; repair the canonical file/name/nesting identity or the shared identity owner. Read the bounded outer_wrapper_code, deepest_stable_cause_code, execution_stage, declared_target, verification_id, test_proof_id, run disposition, blocker/observation code, and truncation facts in the response. Repair a binding or declared test in the controlled proof contract when those facts name the contract boundary; repair the launcher/runtime or reporter/provider prerequisite when they name execution infrastructure. The compact public result returns only the requested subject, one common subject-binding summary, aggregate counts/status, proof and verification identities with status, and minimal reason/recovery facts. It never exposes raw output, stacks, absolute paths, commands, argv, environment, provider payloads, or complete inventories, and never exceeds 65,536 UTF-8 bytes.

routes.note: Retry the same canonical subject only after the structured response's owning prerequisite has been repaired. A retry does not repair the contract, launcher, reporter, provider, candidate, or receipt by itself. Preserve git_sha when the original call selected an exact commit.
